.claude/rules\closed-loop-recursive-narrowing.md:86:Disposition: ship with a `MANUAL-OVERRIDE` marker in the patch site comment AND in the commit/PR body, citing severity, the specific codex finding, and the owner identity. .claude/rules\cross-model-consensus.md:314:- **Trust first T1 verdict hit instead of file END** — codex deep-review-exec outputs span 1k-10k lines and routinely echo the `VERDICT: APPROVE | NEEDS-REVISION | REJECT` template near the start before the actual investigation, then emit the real verdict at EOF. Discipline: `wc -l <file>` first; then `grep -nE "VERDICT:|^F-[0-9]|conf=|confidence|APPROVE|NEEDS-REVISION|REJECT|severity (P[0-3])" <file> | tail -20` (force last hits, not first); then `tail -200 <file>` and confirm the final verdict block is at EOF. Genuine-truncation branch: only call `INCONCLUSIVE-INCOMPLETE` when the last grep hits are prompt-echo / early-investigation AND `tail -200` ends mid-investigation with no final verdict — high line count alone does NOT imply completion. Empirically refuted on iter-17/18/20 completed T1 verdict files (n=3 verdicts at L4457/L10073/L1610 + EOF) plus iter-19 separate skipped-T1 propagation case — total n=4 affected commit-body claims, n=3 verified completed outputs. Failure class: `synthesis-layer-verify.md` §Reporting categories OVER. Operational home: this rule's verdict-reading + fail-closed protocol. Provenance: `feedback_codex_t1_verdict_reading_discipline.md` + iter-21 fix-forward.

.claude/rules\parallel-session-worktree-isolation.md:113:   - **(a) Atomic temp-rename for FULL-FILE writes ONLY**: write to `<path>.tmp.<nanos>.<pid>`, then `os.replace` (cross-platform atomic on POSIX + Windows NTFS). Use ONLY for FULL-FILE write-once classes where last-writer-wins is acceptable (e.g., `codex_review_HEAD_<sha8>.txt` written once per commit, `codex_consult_<topic>_<pid>.txt` written once per consult). For NO-CLOBBER first-write semantics, use `os.open(path, os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | os.O_WRONLY)` for exclusive creation; fail closed (caller catches) if collision detected.
.claude/rules\parallel-session-worktree-isolation.md:114:   - **(b) Filename-namespace**: include `<agent_id8>` or `<process_id>` in filename so concurrent writers cannot collide on the same path (e.g., `codex_review_HEAD_<sha8>_<agent_id8>.txt` or `codex_consult_<topic>_<pid>.txt`). Consumers must merge across the namespace if a unified view is needed.
.claude/rules\parallel-session-worktree-isolation.md:115:   - **(c) Lockfile + O_CREAT|O_APPEND atomic-write for SHARED JSONL append**: open the JSONL log with `os.open(path, os.O_CREAT | os.O_APPEND | os.O_WRONLY, mode)` where `mode` defaults to `0o600` (owner-only — per Round-5b T3 round-3 NEEDS-ATTENTION conf=0.78 NEW-CLASS trust-boundary finding on commit `c2b5dee`: `0o644` was world-readable and leaked audit-trail content (agent prompts, PIDs, verdict cite paths, `agent_id` UUIDs, T1/T2/T3 verdict bodies) on multi-user hosts. Callers MAY opt-in to `0o640` group-readable for shared-CI cases via explicit `mode=` argument + documented umask interaction (e.g., `umask 0o027` for CI runner) — `0o644` is REJECTED as default for any audit-trail JSONL). **Migration semantic for legacy files** *(Round-7 amendment per T3 round-4 NEEDS-ATTENTION conf=0.91 NEW-CLASS finding on commit `df37fb1`; closes non-migrating gap caught by codex GPT-5.5 BRIDGE-MODE — POSIX `os.open` applies `mode` ONLY when `O_CREAT` actually CREATES the file)*: pre-existing files at `0o644` (created under Round-3-through-5 mandates pre-Round-6) RETAIN their world-readable perms after open, leaving the audit-trail leak intact unless coerced. After every `os.open`, the caller MUST: (i) read `current_mode = stat.S_IMODE(os.fstat(fd).st_mode)`; (ii) if `current_mode != mode` AND the file is owned by caller-uid, call `os.fchmod(fd, mode)` to coerce existing file to the mode invariant; (iii) if `os.fchmod` raises (`PermissionError` due to read-only mount, alien owner, ACL conflict on Windows NTFS, etc.), FAIL CLOSED — propagate the exception rather than proceeding with non-conforming perms (the audit-trail invariant is enforced everywhere or fails loudly). Document in commit body for any consumer applying this rule: one-time migration shell command `find .claude/state -name '*.jsonl' -perm /044 -exec chmod 0600 {} +` (POSIX) OR `Get-ChildItem -Path .claude/state -Filter *.jsonl -Recurse | Where-Object { ($_ | Get-Acl).AccessToString -match 'Everyone Allow Read' } | ForEach-Object { icacls $_.FullName /inheritance:r /grant ${env:USERNAME}:F }` (Windows) for legacy `mcp_health.jsonl` / `subagent_transcripts.jsonl` / `codex_postcommit_reviews.jsonl` / `subagent_start.jsonl` / `worktree_lifecycle_audit.jsonl` files created at `0o644` per pre-Round-6 mandates. The `O_CREAT` flag ensures a missing log auto-creates rather than failing the first writer; **if `os.open` raises (read-only mount, permission denied, disk full), the exception MUST propagate — do not catch-and-ignore** (per Round-5 F-1 silent-failure finding). Take an **exclusive advisory lock** (`fcntl.flock(fd, LOCK_EX)` on POSIX / `msvcrt.locking` on Windows); **if neither primitive is available, or if the platform does not enforce advisory locks (e.g., NFS without NLM support), FAIL CLOSED — raise rather than proceeding without a lock** (per Round-5 F-2 NFS-silent-succeed finding). **Windows separate-lockfile mechanism** *(Round-7c per T3 round-7b NEEDS-ATTENTION conf=0.78 NEW-CLASS finding on commit `48c49fb` caught by codex GPT-5.5 BRIDGE-MODE)*: `msvcrt.locking` locks `nbytes` from CURRENT file-pointer position, NOT the whole file like POSIX `fcntl.flock`. Under O_APPEND the JSONL fd's pointer moves on each write, breaking lock-release symmetry (LK_UNLCK at the new pointer would find no lock at the byte LK_LOCK was issued for). Round-7b workaround (shipped at `scripts/_atomic_jsonl_append.py:_acquire_lock(fd, path)` commit `48c49fb`): open separate `<jsonl-path>.lock` file with 1-byte placeholder + lock byte 0 of the LOCKFILE (no writes to lockfile means file pointer stays at byte 0). Module returns `lock_fd` for Windows callers to release; `None` for POSIX. **Lock-protocol rollout constraint** *(Round-7c per same T3 finding)*: when the lock protocol bumps (direct-jsonl-fd → separate-lockfile-v1, or separate-lockfile-v1 → separate-lockfile-v2-versioned), enforce single-version deployment for the entire concurrent-writer cohort. Old + new code locking DIFFERENT lock domains do NOT mutually exclude — concurrent writers can race even though each ALONE acquires its lock correctly. Mitigations (pick ONE before any concurrent rollout): **(i) transitional dual-lock**: acquire both old AND new protocol locks in series during the transition window; **(ii) runtime version-marker**: write protocol-version byte to lockfile + fail-closed on read-version-mismatch (FORWARD-REF for v2 lock protocol bump); **(iii) single-version cohort barrier**: coordinate cohort upgrade via deployment system before any new-version runs. Currently sss has ZERO consumers of `_atomic_jsonl_append.py` (FORWARD-REF wire-up Ships 2-5 pending per `tmp/wave22-orchestrator-salvage-jsonl-mode-bits-audit-2026-05-05.md`), so the version-skew window is THEORETICAL until first hook migrates to use the module. Future protocol bumps MUST honor one of (i)/(ii)/(iii). HOLD the lock across BOTH (a) JSON-encoding the record AND (b) the single low-level `os.write(fd, encoded_bytes)` — never use buffered text writes (`f.write(json.dumps(rec) + "\n")` via Python file objects can split into multiple writes). **If JSON encoding raises (`UnicodeEncodeError`, non-serializable type), release the lock and propagate the exception — do not silently drop the record** (per Round-5 F-3 silent-record-drop finding). For records where **`len(encoded_bytes)` — the byte count AFTER JSON encoding, NOT the key count of the dict —** exceeds the platform atomic-write bound (≤PIPE_BUF 4KB POSIX; ≤512 bytes for Windows or treat the lock as the sole correctness boundary), reject the record OR shard via option (b) filename-namespace; do NOT silently truncate (per Round-5 F-5 measurement-target finding). After the write, `os.fsync(fd)` if durability is part of the contract (audit-trail JSONL needs fsync; ephemeral telemetry may skip); **if `os.fsync` raises (`EIO`, `ENOSPC`), propagate the exception — do not silently ignore a durability failure when durability is contracted** (per Round-5 F-4 fsync-failure finding). Use for SHARED JSONL log targets (`mcp_health.jsonl`, `subagent_transcripts.jsonl`, `codex_postcommit_reviews.jsonl` class) where consumers expect interleaved appends from multiple writers and unified-view semantics are required.

  161:     2. **DUPLICATE-FUNCTIONALITY** — full parallel exists in Anthropic/eee stack covering same scope and mechanism. Disposition: **REJECT-FOR-FIT** per `Z:/claude-sota/.claude/rules/kiss-dry-yagni.md` Must-Never #4 (no duplicate functionality without clear reason).
  162: 
  163:     3. **PARTIAL-OVERLAP** — incumbent and candidate cover overlapping function via DIFFERENT MECHANISMS. Disposition: **CASE-BY-CASE**, typically CITE-PATTERN-ONLY or STUDY-PILOT-PATTERN-EXTRACT. Example: Wave 134 Fire 27-C mem0 (fact-extraction-based memory) vs eee graphiti (temporal-KG-based) vs mcp-memory (sqlite-vec-based) — same memory layer, different mechanisms. Codex T1 verdict at `.claude/state/codex_consult_w134_f27c_mem0_OUT.txt` STUDY-PILOT-PATTERN-EXTRACT conf=0.87.
  164: 
  165:     4. **PROVIDER-COMPLEMENT** — parallel API surfaces but different scopes; both can coexist. Disposition: **INSTALL as ALTERNATIVE (not PRIMARY)** — primary incumbent retains canonical position. Example: Wave 134 Fire 27-A openai-agents-python (vs Anthropic `claude-agent-sdk-python` @ HEAD `b512f256`) — Anthropic SDK = direct CC control plane (PRIMARY); OpenAI SDK = provider-agnostic orchestration (ALTERNATIVE). Codex T1 verdict at `.claude/state/codex_consult_w134_f27a_openai_agents_python_OUT.txt` STUDY-PILOT-PATTERN-EXTRACT conf=0.89.
  166: 
  167:     5. **ECOSYSTEM-IMPORT** — core primitive GENUINELY-NEW at the surface level but imports parallel ecosystem at the dependency level. Disposition: **EVALUATE ecosystem cost vs core primitive value** (often CITE-PATTERN-ONLY when ecosystem footprint disproportionate). Example: Wave 134 Fire 27-B langgraph (Pregel BSP graph execution is novel BUT requires `langchain-core>=1.4.0a2` + 6+ langgraph-* sub-package import + LangSmith proprietary recommended). Pattern B HNF disposition at `.claude/state/codex_consult_w134_f27b_langgraph_OUT.txt`.
  168: 
  169:     6. **CITE-CLASS-CANONICAL** — Anthropic-OFFICIAL educational/reference material (cookbook notebook / official docs / non-runtime / non-install artifact) ALREADY operating as TIER-1 cite reference per existing pin in `research-protocol.md` or equivalent. Distinct from PROVIDER-COMPLEMENT (parallel runtime mechanism) and ECOSYSTEM-IMPORT (core primitive new with ecosystem footprint) by requiring: (a) audited object is REFERENCE material not runtime/install artifact, (b) cite-class adoption is the CORRECT primary mode, (c) correct disposition is RATIFICATION of an existing eee rule/practice against the TIER-1-OFFICIAL primary source. Disposition: **ACCEPT-AS-CITE-REFERENCE** — do NOT install as runtime artifact; ratify existing eee discipline against TIER-1-OFFICIAL primary source; document operational-overlap for future cite-extraction priority queue. Empirical evidence: W152-F20 + F22 + F23 + F24 (n=4 same-arc 2026-05-11) — Anthropic Cookbook overall (F20 commit `4170fbc`) + CMA prompt-versioning ratified FM-21 OWNED rule (F22 commit `4ed6666`) + CMA human-in-loop ratified CR-7 + safety floor (F23 commit `04b1eb4`) + research-agent recipe ratified sota-researcher + multi-source-discovery-breadth (F24 commit `1d35a22`). **Promotion gate**: n=4 same-arc exceeds `Z:/claude-sota/.claude/rules/codification-threshold.md:34-39,76-80` default n=2 confirmation bar (per cycle-321 expected-savings fast-path: ~3-10 min/audit × ~10-20 educational-source audits/month = ~30-200 min/month savings; LOC ≤200 fit).
  170: 
  171:     **Cite class for this 6-class lattice itself**: `constituents=[TIER-3-LOCAL-OPERATOR-DERIVED @ Wave 134 Fire 27-A + 27-B + 27-C codex T1 verdicts, TIER-3-LOCAL-OPERATOR-DERIVED @ W152-F20 + F22 + F23 + F24 same-arc n=4 evidence (commits 4170fbc + 4ed6666 + 04b1eb4 + 1d35a22), TIER-2 @ existing cardinal-rule-12 scaffolding, TIER-2 @ Z:/claude-sota/.claude/rules/citation-discipline.md rule #8 source-class reduction lattice precedent, TIER-1-DIRECT @ Anthropic + OpenAI + LangChain TIER-1 maintainer evidence]; effective_tier=TIER-3-LOCAL-COMPOSITION` per `Z:/claude-sota/.claude/rules/citation-discipline.md` rule #8 MIN_PRECEDENCE.
  172: 
  173:     **Application discipline**:
  174:     - When auditing ANY upstream candidate for eee adoption, FIRST classify per 6-class lattice (after Probe DAG passes); THEN apply class-specific disposition
  175:     - Class assignment is determined by **mechanism comparison** vs incumbent (not surface API similarity alone)
  176:     - **PROVIDER-COMPLEMENT** vs **DUPLICATE-FUNCTIONALITY**: distinguished by whether both incumbents cover DIFFERENT scopes (PROVIDER-COMPLEMENT — both useful) or SAME scope (DUPLICATE — pick one)
  177:     - **PARTIAL-OVERLAP** vs **PROVIDER-COMPLEMENT**: distinguished by whether the DIFFERENT MECHANISMS suggest parallel co-existence (PROVIDER-COMPLEMENT) or competing-implementations (PARTIAL-OVERLAP requires case-by-case)
  178:     - **ECOSYSTEM-IMPORT** is the OPERATIONAL escape valve when a candidate's core primitive is novel but ecosystem footprint creates duplicate-frameworks concern
  179:     - **CITE-CLASS-CANONICAL** applies ONLY when the audited object itself is educational/reference material (NOT runtime/install artifact); having a cite anchor is NOT sufficient — PROVIDER-COMPLEMENT and ECOSYSTEM-IMPORT candidates can also have parallel cite anchors. The discriminator is "is the object itself an install-class artifact or reference material?"

  285: 
  286: ### How and when to invoke skills (mandatory discipline)
  287: 
  288: **For Claude (main thread)**:
  289: - Per `using-superpowers` 1% rule: invoke ANY relevant skill BEFORE response or action. Skill check comes BEFORE clarifying questions / file exploration / planning.
  290: - Multiple skills: Process skills (brainstorming / debugging / verification-before-completion) determine HOW; Implementation skills (frontend-design / api-and-interface-design / TDD) guide EXECUTION. Layer them when both apply.
  291: - Announce: "Using [skill] to [purpose]" before each invocation per `using-superpowers` skill flow digraph.
  292: - Follow skill EXACTLY when rigid (TDD / debugging); adapt principles when flexible (patterns).
  293: 
  294: **For subagents** (per CCBP `claude-subagents.md:32-34` `skills:` preload field):
  295: - Subagent briefs MUST include skill-awareness clause when role demands. Standing directive `Z:/claude-sota/.claude/rules/advanced-agent-team-standing-directive.md` invariant applies — agent briefs cite TIER-1 sources at file:line + HEAD SHA, including relevant SKILL.md files for the agent's role.
  296: - Subagent frontmatter `skills:` field can preload specific skills (CC 2.1+); `allowed-tools` controls tool surface; `context: fork` runs in isolated subagent context per CCBP 15-field spec.
  297: - Common preload pairings:
  298:   - `sota-researcher` agent → preload `deep-research` + `research-ops` ECC skills + `iterative-retrieval` + `using-agent-skills` (auto-fires regardless via discovery)
  299:   - `architect` agent → preload `code-architect` + `agent-harness-construction` + `agentic-engineering` ECC skills
  300:   - `code-reviewer` agent → preload `code-review-and-quality` (addy) + `silent-failure-hunter` (ECC) + `requesting-code-review` / `receiving-code-review` (superpowers)
  301:   - `debugger` agent → preload `systematic-debugging` (superpowers) + `debugging-and-error-recovery` (addy) + `agent-introspection-debugging` (ECC)
  302:   - `verifier` agent → preload `verification-before-completion` (superpowers) + `eval-harness` (ECC)
  303: 
  304: **For multi-skill orchestration** (chained or layered):
  305: - **Chain example**: brainstorming → writing-plans → subagent-driven-development → test-driven-development → requesting-code-review → finishing-a-development-branch (per superpowers workflow grammar L7 sequence)
  306: - **Layer example**: while implementing a feature: `feature-dev` (claude-plugins-official) PLUS `incremental-implementation` (addy) PLUS `tdd` (superpowers) PLUS `safety-guard` (ECC) PLUS `verification-before-completion` (superpowers)
  307: - **Anti-pattern**: invoking ONLY one skill when 2-4 apply. The 1% rule is bidirectional — even if uncertain whether skill X applies, invoke it; if it turns out wrong, drop it.

  322: # Plugin name format: '<plugin>@<marketplace>'. Cache layout: .claude/plugins/cache/<marketplace>/<plugin>/<version>/
  323: # where <version> may be semver (5.1.0) OR content-hash (70d57685d411). Dynamic discovery removes hardcoded version-string drift hazard (CR-9 D6 today-release-auto-upgrade defense).

Cite class downgraded to TIER-1-NAMED-AUTHOR-QUOTE-PROVISIONAL with REQUIRED metadata: (a) ISBN/DOI + page + verbatim-quote inline; (b) verifier-identity disclosure (who-verified-when, e.g., `[VERIFIED 2026-05-04 by orchestrator against book Tip #15 verbatim text]`); (c) explicit `non-automatable: true` marker so review hooks know to defer to human sign-off; (d) **HARD-GATE ELIGIBILITY TEST** *(Round-3 amendment a per T3 R3 NEEDS-ATTENTION conf=0.82 same-class finding on commit `1b87a6e`; supersedes round-2 "MUST prefer" soft preference framing — preference is not gateable; eligibility is)*: PROVISIONAL admission is admissible ONLY when DOI landing page + accessible PDF / publisher excerpt / archived scan (license-permitting) was SEARCHED AND UNAVAILABLE. Mere preference is INSUFFICIENT — if any auditable surrogate exists (DOI/PDF/excerpt/scan), use it as the normative source instead of the physical-only book cite. e.g., ACM DOI `https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/<doi>` for ACM papers IS auditable when paywall-free. .claude/rules\parallel-session-worktree-isolation.md:115:   - **(c) Lockfile + O_CREAT|O_APPEND atomic-write for SHARED JSONL append**: open the JSONL log with `os.open(path, os.O_CREAT | os.O_APPEND | os.O_WRONLY, mode)` where `mode` defaults to `0o600` (owner-only — per Round-5b T3 round-3 NEEDS-ATTENTION conf=0.78 NEW-CLASS trust-boundary finding on commit `c2b5dee`: `0o644` was world-readable and leaked audit-trail content (agent prompts, PIDs, verdict cite paths, `agent_id` UUIDs, T1/T2/T3 verdict bodies) on multi-user hosts. Callers MAY opt-in to `0o640` group-readable for shared-CI cases via explicit `mode=` argument + documented umask interaction (e.g., `umask 0o027` for CI runner) — `0o644` is REJECTED as default for any audit-trail JSONL). **Migration semantic for legacy files** *(Round-7 amendment per T3 round-4 NEEDS-ATTENTION conf=0.91 NEW-CLASS finding on commit `df37fb1`; closes non-migrating gap caught by codex GPT-5.5 BRIDGE-MODE — POSIX `os.open` applies `mode` ONLY when `O_CREAT` actually CREATES the file)*: pre-existing files at `0o644` (created under Round-3-through-5 mandates pre-Round-6) RETAIN their world-readable perms after open, leaving the audit-trail leak intact unless coerced. After every `os.open`, the caller MUST: (i) read `current_mode = stat.S_IMODE(os.fstat(fd).st_mode)`; (ii) if `current_mode != mode` AND the file is owned by caller-uid, call `os.fchmod(fd, mode)` to coerce existing file to the mode invariant; (iii) if `os.fchmod` raises (`PermissionError` due to read-only mount, alien owner, ACL conflict on Windows NTFS, etc.), FAIL CLOSED — propagate the exception rather than proceeding with non-conforming perms (the audit-trail invariant is enforced everywhere or fails loudly). Document in commit body for any consumer applying this rule: one-time migration shell command `find .claude/state -name '*.jsonl' -perm /044 -exec chmod 0600 {} +` (POSIX) OR `Get-ChildItem -Path .claude/state -Filter *.jsonl -Recurse | Where-Object { ($_ | Get-Acl).AccessToString -match 'Everyone Allow Read' } | ForEach-Object { icacls $_.FullName /inheritance:r /grant ${env:USERNAME}:F }` (Windows) for legacy `mcp_health.jsonl` / `subagent_transcripts.jsonl` / `codex_postcommit_reviews.jsonl` / `subagent_start.jsonl` / `worktree_lifecycle_audit.jsonl` files created at `0o644` per pre-Round-6 mandates. The `O_CREAT` flag ensures a missing log auto-creates rather than failing the first writer; **if `os.open` raises (read-only mount, permission denied, disk full), the exception MUST propagate — do not catch-and-ignore** (per Round-5 F-1 silent-failure finding). Take an **exclusive advisory lock** (`fcntl.flock(fd, LOCK_EX)` on POSIX / `msvcrt.locking` on Windows); **if neither primitive is available, or if the platform does not enforce advisory locks (e.g., NFS without NLM support), FAIL CLOSED — raise rather than proceeding without a lock** (per Round-5 F-2 NFS-silent-succeed finding). **Windows separate-lockfile mechanism** *(Round-7c per T3 round-7b NEEDS-ATTENTION conf=0.78 NEW-CLASS finding on commit `48c49fb` caught by codex GPT-5.5 BRIDGE-MODE)*: `msvcrt.locking` locks `nbytes` from CURRENT file-pointer position, NOT the whole file like POSIX `fcntl.flock`. Under O_APPEND the JSONL fd's pointer moves on each write, breaking lock-release symmetry (LK_UNLCK at the new pointer would find no lock at the byte LK_LOCK was issued for). Round-7b workaround (shipped at `scripts/_atomic_jsonl_append.py:_acquire_lock(fd, path)` commit `48c49fb`): open separate `<jsonl-path>.lock` file with 1-byte placeholder + lock byte 0 of the LOCKFILE (no writes to lockfile means file pointer stays at byte 0). Module returns `lock_fd` for Windows callers to release; `None` for POSIX. **Lock-protocol rollout constraint** *(Round-7c per same T3 finding)*: when the lock protocol bumps (direct-jsonl-fd → separate-lockfile-v1, or separate-lockfile-v1 → separate-lockfile-v2-versioned), enforce single-version deployment for the entire concurrent-writer cohort. Old + new code locking DIFFERENT lock domains do NOT mutually exclude — concurrent writers can race even though each ALONE acquires its lock correctly. Mitigations (pick ONE before any concurrent rollout): **(i) transitional dual-lock**: acquire both old AND new protocol locks in series during the transition window; **(ii) runtime version-marker**: write protocol-version byte to lockfile + fail-closed on read-version-mismatch (FORWARD-REF for v2 lock protocol bump); **(iii) single-version cohort barrier**: coordinate cohort upgrade via deployment system before any new-version runs. Currently sss has ZERO consumers of `_atomic_jsonl_append.py` (FORWARD-REF wire-up Ships 2-5 pending per `tmp/wave22-orchestrator-salvage-jsonl-mode-bits-audit-2026-05-05.md`), so the version-skew window is THEORETICAL until first hook migrates to use the module. Future protocol bumps MUST honor one of (i)/(ii)/(iii). HOLD the lock across BOTH (a) JSON-encoding the record AND (b) the single low-level `os.write(fd, encoded_bytes)` — never use buffered text writes (`f.write(json.dumps(rec) + "\n")` via Python file objects can split into multiple writes). **If JSON encoding raises (`UnicodeEncodeError`, non-serializable type), release the lock and propagate the exception — do not silently drop the record** (per Round-5 F-3 silent-record-drop finding). For records where **`len(encoded_bytes)` — the byte count AFTER JSON encoding, NOT the key count of the dict —** exceeds the platform atomic-write bound (≤PIPE_BUF 4KB POSIX; ≤512 bytes for Windows or treat the lock as the sole correctness boundary), reject the record OR shard via option (b) filename-namespace; do NOT silently truncate (per Round-5 F-5 measurement-target finding). After the write, `os.fsync(fd)` if durability is part of the contract (audit-trail JSONL needs fsync; ephemeral telemetry may skip); **if `os.fsync` raises (`EIO`, `ENOSPC`), propagate the exception — do not silently ignore a durability failure when durability is contracted** (per Round-5 F-4 fsync-failure finding). Use for SHARED JSONL log targets (`mcp_health.jsonl`, `subagent_transcripts.jsonl`, `codex_postcommit_reviews.jsonl` class) where consumers expect interleaved appends from multiple writers and unified-view semantics are required.

  185: def _classify_parse_failure(raw_output: str, stderr_tail: str) -> str:
  186:     """Sub-classify parse failures (Agent Y task spec, 11-class telemetry).
  187: 
  188:     Cycle-after-iter50.55 ship: prior code lumped all "no-verdict" outcomes
  189:     under a single `parse_failure` status, which made forensic diagnosis
  190:     require manual `jq .stderr_tail` reading every time. Specific subclasses:
  191: 
  192:     - parse_failure_cli_argv_rejected: codex died on argv parse (e.g. -C/-color
  193:       against codex exec review subcommand). Highest-priority class because
  194:       this is a HOOK BUG, not a codex output problem — fix the cmd list.
  195:     - parse_failure_cli_error: codex exited with stderr "error:" but argv
  196:       parsed (likely runtime error like missing auth or sandbox conflict).
  197:     - parse_failure_empty_output: codex completed (or died silently) without
  198:       writing anything to --output-last-message. Likely process killed mid-run
  199:       OR file write race. Inspect process exit code separately.
  200:     - parse_failure_no_json_block: OUT file has content but doesn't start with
  201:       JSON markers `{` or `[`. Likely codex schema regression where verdict is
  202:       now plain text or banner-prefixed.
  203:     - parse_failure_malformed_json: OUT file has content starting with `{` or
  204:       `[` but json.loads() raised JSONDecodeError. Likely truncation or
  205:       embedded control chars.
  206:     - parse_failure_non_dict_root: OUT file parsed to a JSON list/scalar/null
  207:       instead of dict. Codex schema regression.
  208:     - parse_failure_missing_verdict_key: OUT file is a dict but lacks "verdict"
  209:       key. Codex output schema rename (e.g. "decision", "outcome") OR codex
  210:       emitted a partial event instead of the final verdict.
  211: 
  212:     Returns one of the above subclass names. Caller emits to JSONL telemetry
  213:     `status` field for grep-able forensic visibility.
  214:     """
  215:     s = stderr_tail or ""
  216:     r = (raw_output or "").strip()
  217:     if not r:
  218:         if "unexpected argument" in s or "Usage:" in s:
  219:             return "parse_failure_cli_argv_rejected"
  220:         if "error:" in s.lower():
  221:             return "parse_failure_cli_error"
  222:         return "parse_failure_empty_output"
  223:     if not (r.startswith("{") or r.startswith("[")):
  224:         return "parse_failure_no_json_block"
  225:     try:
  226:         data = json.loads(r)
  227:     except json.JSONDecodeError:
  228:         return "parse_failure_malformed_json"
  229:     if not isinstance(data, dict):
  230:         return "parse_failure_non_dict_root"
  231:     if "verdict" not in data:
  232:         return "parse_failure_missing_verdict_key"
  233:     return "parse_failure_unknown"

  236: def _resolve_target_root(cmd: str, payload_cwd: str) -> Path:
  237:     """Find the repo root the commit actually ran in.

  385: def _normalize(file_path: str) -> str:
  386:     if not file_path:
  387:         return ""
  388:     norm = file_path.replace("\\", "/")
  389:     if len(norm) >= 2 and norm[1] == ":":
  390:         norm = norm[:2].lower() + norm[2:]
  391:     return norm
  392: 
  393: 
  394: def _to_repo_relpath(norm_path: str) -> str | None:
  395:     """Return path relative to _PROJECT_ROOT, POSIX-style, or None if outside.
  396: 
  397:     Used by P0-1 exclusion matching: the exclusion globs are written relative
  398:     to repo root (e.g. ".claude/state/**", "data/**"). Matching against the
  399:     raw absolute path would never hit; we strip the repo-root prefix first.
  400:     """
  401:     if not norm_path:
  402:         return None
  403:     repo_norm = _normalize(str(_PROJECT_ROOT))
  404:     if norm_path == repo_norm:
  405:         return ""
  406:     prefix = repo_norm + "/"
  407:     if norm_path.startswith(prefix):
  408:         return norm_path[len(prefix):]
  409:     return None
  410: 
  411: 
  412: def _glob_matches(rel_path: str, pattern: str) -> bool:
  413:     """Match a relative POSIX path against a glob with ** semantics.
  414: 
  415:     fnmatch.fnmatch alone treats `**` as a single-segment glob. For our
  416:     exclusion patterns, `prefix/**` should match every descendant. Strategy:
  417:     - If pattern endswith `/**`, also match exact-prefix
  418:     - Else fall back to fnmatch
  419:     """
  420:     if pattern.endswith("/**"):
  421:         prefix = pattern[: -len("/**")]
  422:         if rel_path == prefix or rel_path.startswith(prefix + "/"):
  423:             return True
  424:     if "**" in pattern:
  425:         # Replace ** with * for fnmatch (fnmatch treats them similarly anyway,
  426:         # but explicit conversion avoids surprises with multi-** patterns).
  427:         flat = pattern.replace("**", "*")
  428:         return fnmatch.fnmatch(rel_path, flat)
  429:     return fnmatch.fnmatch(rel_path, pattern)
  430: 
  431: 
  432: def _path_excluded(target_path: str) -> tuple[bool, str | None]:
  433:     """P0-1: return (is_excluded, exclusion_reason).
  434: 
  435:     Per codex T1 verdict design_recommendations.P0-1_universal_scope.exclusion_set
  436:     + scope:"sss-installed-runtime" + final entry "any resolved path outside the
  437:     repo root" (sibling-derived from Z:/claude-sota verdict; _PROJECT_ROOT resolves
  438:     runtime root via parents[3] so this hook is sibling-portable per Wave 50 fire 24).
  439:     """
  440:     norm = _normalize(target_path)
  441:     if not norm:
  442:         return True, "empty_target_path"
  443: 
  444:     norm_lc = norm.lower()
  445:     if norm_lc.startswith(_CROSS_PROJECT_DEPS_PREFIX):
  446:         return True, "cross_project_deps_tree"
  447: 
  448:     rel = _to_repo_relpath(norm)
  449:     if rel is None:
  450:         return True, _OUTSIDE_REPO_EXCLUSION_REASON
  451: 
  452:     # Ship #314.2 precedence guard: ALWAYS-GATED patterns win over
  453:     # _UNIVERSAL_EXCLUSIONS. Returning (False, None) here means "this path
  454:     # matches a documented gated pattern (sota / audit / feature-handoff
  455:     # verdict surfaces); T1 MUST fire regardless of any later exclusion
  456:     # match". Closes Ship #314 → #314.1 → #314.2 closed-loop arc per
  457:     # .claude/rules/closed-loop-recursive-narrowing.md Round-3 fix-iteration.
  458:     for pattern in _ALWAYS_GATED_PATTERNS:
  459:         if _glob_matches(rel, pattern):
  460:             return False, None
  461: 
  462:     for pattern in _UNIVERSAL_EXCLUSIONS:
  463:         if _glob_matches(rel, pattern):
  464:             return True, f"glob:{pattern}"
  465:     return False, None

  471: def _payload_canonical(tool_input: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
  472:     """Stable string form of tool_input for SHA-12 fingerprint.
  473: 
  474:     Uses sort_keys=True so order shifts in the dict don't bust the SHA. Strips
  475:     keys that vary across retries (none today, but future-proof comment).
  476:     """
  477:     try:
  478:         return json.dumps(tool_input, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False)
  479:     except (TypeError, ValueError):
  480:         return str(tool_input)

  483: def _sha12(s: str) -> str:
  484:     return hashlib.sha256(s.encode("utf-8", errors="replace")).hexdigest()[:12]
  485: 
  486: 
  487: def _slugify_relpath(rel_path: str | None) -> str:
  488:     """Stable, filesystem-safe slug derived from repo-relative path.
  489: 
  490:     Empty/None -> "_root". Replaces / with __ and strips chars not in
  491:     [a-zA-Z0-9_.-]. Bounded to 60 chars to keep filenames manageable.
  492:     """
  493:     if not rel_path:
  494:         return "_root"
  495:     candidate = rel_path.replace("/", "__")
  496:     candidate = re.sub(r"[^a-zA-Z0-9_.-]", "_", candidate)
  497:     return candidate[:60] or "_unnamed"

  520: def _try_acquire_lock(lock_path: Path, spawn_pid: int | None) -> bool:
  521:     """Atomically acquire lockfile via O_CREAT|O_EXCL. Returns True if acquired.
  522: 
  523:     Lock contents: JSON {pid, ts, host}. PID is the spawned codex Popen pid
  524:     (or 0 if mock/dry-run). Used by retry path to detect stale locks.
  525:     """
  526:     try:
  527:         lock_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
  528:         fd = os.open(str(lock_path), os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | os.O_WRONLY, 0o644)
  529:         try:
  530:             payload = json.dumps({
  531:                 "pid": spawn_pid if spawn_pid is not None else 0,
  532:                 "ts": _now_iso(),
  533:                 "host": os.environ.get("COMPUTERNAME") or os.environ.get("HOSTNAME") or "",
  534:             }).encode("utf-8")
  535:             os.write(fd, payload)
  536:         finally:
  537:             os.close(fd)
  538:         return True
  539:     except FileExistsError:
  540:         return False
  541:     except OSError as exc:
  542:         log_swallow(exc, f"codex_t1_gate.lock_acquire:{lock_path.name}")
  543:         return False
  544:

  546: def _release_lock(lock_path: Path) -> None:
  547:     try:
  548:         lock_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
  549:     except OSError as exc:
  550:         log_swallow(exc, f"codex_t1_gate.lock_release:{lock_path.name}")

  571: def _with_bucket_lock(lock_path: Path, fn) -> bool:
  572:     """Execute fn() under O_CREAT|O_EXCL lock with bounded retry.
  573: 
  574:     Returns True if fn() ran (lock acquired), False if gave up after timeout.
  575:     """
  576:     deadline = time.time() + 5.0
  577:     while time.time() < deadline:
  578:         try:
  579:             lock_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
  580:             fd = os.open(str(lock_path), os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | os.O_WRONLY, 0o644)
  581:             try:
  582:                 os.write(fd, str(os.getpid()).encode("utf-8"))
  583:             finally:
  584:                 os.close(fd)
  585:             try:
  586:                 fn()
  587:             finally:
  588:                 try:
  589:                     lock_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
  590:                 except OSError as exc:
  591:                     log_swallow(exc, f"codex_t1_gate.bucket_lock_release:{lock_path.name}")
  592:             return True
  593:         except FileExistsError:
  594:             time.sleep(0.05)
  595:         except OSError as exc:
  596:             log_swallow(exc, f"codex_t1_gate.bucket_lock_acquire:{lock_path.name}")
  597:             return False
  598:     return False

  311: def _parse_stdin() -> dict[str, Any]:

  318:             return {}

  337: # FM-12 fix-forward (codex T1 verdict 2026-05-03 NEEDS-REVISION at

  371: def _parse_commit_pathspecs(cmd_str: str) -> list[str] | None:
  372:     """Extract pathspec scope from `git commit -o/--only` form in a Bash command.
  373: 
  374:     PRECEDENCE policy per codex T1 verdict on FM-12 fix-forward 2026-05-03:
  375:     parsed pathspec is AUTHORITATIVE scope when -o/--only detected (per
  376:     https://git-scm.com/docs/git-commit `--only` docs: "commit only the
  377:     specified paths, disregarding staged contents for other paths"). Returns:
  378:       - None: no -o/--only flag detected → caller falls back to staged diff
  379:       - list[str] (possibly empty): -o/--only detected; list is authoritative
  380:         (empty when --only used without inline pathspecs e.g. --pathspec-from-file)
  381: 
  382:     Closes FM-12 timing race (n=3 same-arc evidence Ship #243-H + #3a.3 +
  383:     Probe-7): PreToolUse fires BEFORE single-shell `git add foo && git commit
  384:     -o foo` chain runs, so `git diff --cached` returns 0 in-scope files at
  385:     hook fire time. Parsed pathspec from cmd_str gives correct scope.
  386: 
  387:     Algorithmic precedent: _guard_base.git_verb_matches:261-309 (shlex.split
  388:     on shell-op-split segments, value-flag walk for global pre-verb flags).
  389:     """
  390:     if not cmd_str or "commit" not in cmd_str:
  391:         return None
  392: 
  393:     found_only = False
  394:     forced_review = False  # Round-2: --only + --pathspec-from-file* combo detected
  395:     pathspecs: list[str] = []
  396: 
  397:     # Split on shell ops to handle compound chains (&&, ||, ;)
  398:     for seg in re.split(r"\s*(?:&&|\|\||;)\s*", cmd_str.strip()):
  399:         seg = seg.strip()
  400:         if not seg.startswith("git "):
  401:             continue
  402:         try:
  403:             parts = shlex.split(seg, posix=True)
  404:         except ValueError:
  405:             parts = seg.split()
  406:         if not parts or parts[0] != "git":
  407:             continue
  408: 
  409:         # Walk past global pre-verb flags (e.g. -C <root>, -c key=val) per
  410:         # _guard_base.git_verb_matches algorithm
  411:         idx = 1
  412:         while idx < len(parts):
  413:             tok = parts[idx]
  414:             if tok in _GIT_FLAGS_VALUE:
  415:                 idx += 2
  416:                 continue
  417:             if tok in _GIT_FLAGS_NOVALUE:
  418:                 idx += 1
  419:                 continue
  420:             if tok.startswith("--") and "=" in tok:
  421:                 idx += 1
  422:                 continue
  423:             break
  424: 
  425:         # Verb must be "commit" — else this segment doesn't matter
  426:         if idx >= len(parts) or parts[idx] != "commit":
  427:             continue
  428:         idx += 1  # past "commit" token
  429: 
  430:         # Parse commit args
  431:         seg_only = False
  432:         seg_paths: list[str] = []
  433:         seg_pathspec_from_file = False  # Round-2: detect --only + --pathspec-from-file* combo
  434:         after_dash_dash = False
  435: 
  436:         while idx < len(parts):
  437:             tok = parts[idx]
  438: 
  439:             # Everything after `--` is pathspec (even tokens starting with `-`)
  440:             if after_dash_dash:
  441:                 seg_paths.append(tok)
  442:                 idx += 1
  443:                 continue
  444: 
  445:             if tok == "--":
  446:                 after_dash_dash = True
  447:                 idx += 1
  448:                 continue
  449: 
  450:             # -o / --only flag: collect inline pathspecs (consecutive non-flag tokens)
  451:             if tok in ("-o", "--only"):
  452:                 seg_only = True
  453:                 idx += 1
  454:                 while idx < len(parts) and not parts[idx].startswith("-"):
  455:                     seg_paths.append(parts[idx])
  456:                     idx += 1
  457:                 continue
  458: 
  459:             # Round-2 (T3 HIGH severity at .claude/state/codex_review_HEAD_e5a008cd.txt):
  460:             # detect file-backed pathspec forms BEFORE the value-skip / flag=value
  461:             # short-circuits below consume them invisibly. When combined with --only,
  462:             # parser cannot statically resolve the pathspec content (file is read at
  463:             # commit time) — set seg_pathspec_from_file flag for FAIL-CLOSED sentinel.
  464:             if tok == "--pathspec-from-file" or tok.startswith("--pathspec-from-file="):
  465:                 seg_pathspec_from_file = True
  466:                 # fall through to standard skip handling below
  467:             if tok == "--pathspec-file-nul":
  468:                 # Boolean modifier (no value); explicit skip since not in _COMMIT_FLAGS_VALUE.
  469:                 # No standalone effect on scope, but combined with --pathspec-from-file
  470:                 # signals NUL-separated file format; flag already set above if present.
  471:                 idx += 1
  472:                 continue
  473: 
  474:             # Skip --flag=value form (single token; e.g. --message=foo)
  475:             if tok.startswith("--") and "=" in tok:
  476:                 idx += 1
  477:                 continue
  478: 
  479:             # Skip value-taking commit options (consume flag + next token as value)
  480:             if tok in _COMMIT_FLAGS_VALUE:
  481:                 idx += 2
  482:                 continue
  483: 
  484:             # Skip other boolean flags
  485:             if tok.startswith("-"):
  486:                 idx += 1
  487:                 continue
  488: 
  489:             # Non-flag positional token outside `-o`/`--only`/`--`: per
  490:             # `git commit <paths>` docs paths-without-flag are equivalent to
  491:             # `--only` BUT current ship scope is explicit -o/--only forms only
  492:             # (codex T1 Q3 edge-case note for next-fire extension if telemetry
  493:             # shows this form in use).
  494:             idx += 1
  495: 
  496:         if seg_only:
  497:             found_only = True
  498:             pathspecs.extend(seg_paths)
  499:         if seg_pathspec_from_file:
  500:             # Round-3 fix-forward (T3 HIGH at .claude/state/codex_review_HEAD_ff0dccfd.txt):
  501:             # --pathspec-from-file* makes file-listed paths the commit scope
  502:             # EVEN WITHOUT explicit --only flag. Per git-commit man page:
  503:             # paths-without-flag are equivalent to --only ("If you specify
  504:             # paths on the command line, then this option behaves as if
  505:             # --only were also specified"). Sentinel MUST fire on ANY

   84:         return "\n".join(e.get("new_string", "") for e in edits if isinstance(e, dict))
   85:     return None
   86: 
   87: 
   88: def _scan(text: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
   89:     """Return [(rule_name, masked_fragment), ...]."""
   90:     findings: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
   91:     for name, pat in _RULES:
   92:         m = pat.search(text)
   93:         if m:
   94:             frag = m.group(0)
   95:             # Mask the middle of the match before stderr/log
   96:             masked = frag if len(frag) <= 12 else f"{frag[:4]}…{frag[-4:]}"
   97:             findings.append((name, masked))
   98:     return findings
   99: 
  100: 
  101: def main() -> int:
  102:     payload = read_stdin_payload("SECRET_SCAN_DISABLE", _CTX)
  103:     if payload is None:
  104:         return 0
  105:     tool = payload.get("tool_name")
  106:     if tool not in _WATCHED_TOOLS:
  107:         return 0
  108:     content = _extract_content(payload)
  109:     if not content:
  110:         return 0
  111: 
  112:     findings = _scan(content)
  113:     if not findings:
  114:         return 0
  115: 
  116:     file_hint = (payload.get("tool_input") or {}).get("file_path", "<unknown-path>")

  121:     if _STRICT:

  125:         }))
  126:         return 2
  127: 
  128:     print("[secret_scan_guard] WARN-mode — edit allowed; set SECRET_SCAN_STRICT=1 to block.", file=sys.stderr)
  129:     return 0
  130:

  133:     sys.exit(main())

    1: ---
    2: name: verification-before-completion
    3: description: Use when about to claim work is complete, fixed, or passing, before committing or creating PRs - requires running verification commands and confirming output before making any success claims; evidence before assertions always
    4: ---
    5: 
    6: # Verification Before Completion
    7: 
    8: ## Overview
    9: 
   10: Claiming work is complete without verification is dishonesty, not efficiency.
   11: 
   12: **Core principle:** Evidence before claims, always.
   13: 
   14: **Violating the letter of this rule is violating the spirit of this rule.**
   15: 
   16: ## The Iron Law
   17: 
   18: ```
   19: NO COMPLETION CLAIMS WITHOUT FRESH VERIFICATION EVIDENCE
   20: ```
   21: 
   22: If you haven't run the verification command in this message, you cannot claim it passes.
   23: 
   24: ## The Gate Function
   25: 
   26: ```
   27: BEFORE claiming any status or expressing satisfaction:
   28: 
   29: 1. IDENTIFY: What command proves this claim?
   30: 2. RUN: Execute the FULL command (fresh, complete)
   31: 3. READ: Full output, check exit code, count failures
   32: 4. VERIFY: Does output confirm the claim?
   33:    - If NO: State actual status with evidence
   34:    - If YES: State claim WITH evidence
   35: 5. ONLY THEN: Make the claim
   36: 
   37: Skip any step = lying, not verifying
   38: ```
   39: 
   40: ## Common Failures
   41: 
   42: | Claim | Requires | Not Sufficient |
   43: |-------|----------|----------------|
   44: | Tests pass | Test command output: 0 failures | Previous run, "should pass" |
   45: | Linter clean | Linter output: 0 errors | Partial check, extrapolation |
   46: | Build succeeds | Build command: exit 0 | Linter passing, logs look good |
   47: | Bug fixed | Test original symptom: passes | Code changed, assumed fixed |
   48: | Regression test works | Red-green cycle verified | Test passes once |
   49: | Agent completed | VCS diff shows changes | Agent reports "success" |
   50: | Requirements met | Line-by-line checklist | Tests passing |
   51: 
   52: ## Red Flags - STOP
   53: 
   54: - Using "should", "probably", "seems to"
   55: - Expressing satisfaction before verification ("Great!", "Perfect!", "Done!", etc.)
   56: - About to commit/push/PR without verification
   57: - Trusting agent success reports
   58: - Relying on partial verification
   59: - Thinking "just this once"
   60: - Tired and wanting work over
   61: - **ANY wording implying success without having run verification**
   62: 
   63: ## Rationalization Prevention
   64: 
   65: | Excuse | Reality |
   66: |--------|---------|
   67: | "Should work now" | RUN the verification |
   68: | "I'm confident" | Confidence ≠ evidence |
   69: | "Just this once" | No exceptions |
   70: | "Linter passed" | Linter ≠ compiler |
   71: | "Agent said success" | Verify independently |
   72: | "I'm tired" | Exhaustion ≠ excuse |
   73: | "Partial check is enough" | Partial proves nothing |
   74: | "Different words so rule doesn't apply" | Spirit over letter |
   75: 
   76: ## Key Patterns
   77: 
   78: **Tests:**
   79: ```
   80: ✅ [Run test command] [See: 34/34 pass] "All tests pass"

 succeeded in 403ms:

   52: _RE_NO_VERIFY = re.compile(r"--no-verify\b")
   53: _RE_COMMIT_N_SHORT_A = re.compile(r"\s-n(?:\s|$)")
   54: _RE_COMMIT_N_SHORT_B = re.compile(r"\s-n[a-zA-Z]")
   55: _RE_HOOKS_PATH = re.compile(r"-c\s+[\"']?core\.hooksPath\s*=")
   56: _RE_WS = re.compile(r"\s")
   57: _RE_SUBCMD_AFTER_CHAR = re.compile(r"[\s;&#|>)\]}\"']")
   58: _RE_SEMI_OR_PIPE = re.compile(r"[;|]")
   59: 
   60: 
   61: def _is_in_comment(s: str, idx: int) -> bool:
   62:     """Is position `idx` inside a shell comment (unescaped `#`)."""
   63:     line_start = s.rfind("\n", 0, idx) + 1
   64:     before = s[line_start:idx]
   65:     for i, ch in enumerate(before):
   66:         if ch == "#":
   67:             prev = before[i - 1] if i > 0 else ""
   68:             if prev != "$" and prev != "\\":
   69:                 return True
   70:     return False
   71: 
   72: 
   73: def _find_git(s: str, start: int) -> tuple[int, int] | None:
   74:     """Find next 'git' token (or 'git.exe') starting at `start`. Returns (index, len) or None."""
   75:     pos = start
   76:     while pos < len(s):
   77:         idx = s.find("git", pos)
   78:         if idx == -1:
   79:             return None
   80:         is_exe = s[idx + 3 : idx + 7].lower() == ".exe"
   81:         length = 7 if is_exe else 3
   82:         after = s[idx + length] if idx + length < len(s) else " "
   83:         if not (after in " \t\n\r\"'" or _RE_WS.match(after)):
   84:             pos = idx + 1
   85:             continue
   86:         before = s[idx - 1] if idx > 0 else " "
   87:         if before in _VALID_BEFORE_GIT:
   88:             return (idx, length)
   89:         pos = idx + 1
   90:     return None
   91: 
   92: 
   93: def _detect_git_command(s: str) -> tuple[str, int] | None:
   94:     """Return (subcommand, offset-after-subcommand) or None.
   95: 
   96:     Picks the subcommand nearest to 'git' so `git push origin commit` does not
   97:     misclassify 'commit' as the subcommand.
   98:     """
   99:     start = 0
  100:     while start < len(s):
  101:         git_hit = _find_git(s, start)
  102:         if not git_hit:
  103:             return None
  104:         git_idx, git_len = git_hit
  105: 
  106:         if _is_in_comment(s, git_idx):
  107:             start = git_idx + git_len
  108:             continue
  109: 
  110:         best_cmd: str | None = None
  111:         best_idx = len(s) + 1
  112: 
  113:         for cmd in _GIT_COMMANDS_WITH_NO_VERIFY:
  114:             search_pos = git_idx + git_len
  115:             while search_pos < len(s):
  116:                 cmd_idx = s.find(cmd, search_pos)
  117:                 if cmd_idx == -1:
  118:                     break
  119:                 before = s[cmd_idx - 1] if cmd_idx > 0 else " "
  120:                 after = s[cmd_idx + len(cmd)] if cmd_idx + len(cmd) < len(s) else " "
  121:                 if not _RE_WS.match(before):
  122:                     search_pos = cmd_idx + 1
  123:                     continue
  124:                 if after != "" and not _RE_SUBCMD_AFTER_CHAR.match(after):
  125:                     search_pos = cmd_idx + 1
  126:                     continue
  127:                 if _RE_SEMI_OR_PIPE.search(s[git_idx + git_len : cmd_idx]):
  128:                     break
  129:                 if _is_in_comment(s, cmd_idx):
  130:                     search_pos = cmd_idx + 1
  131:                     continue
  132: 
  133:                 # verify tokens between 'git' and the candidate are only flags or flag-arguments
  134:                 gap = s[git_idx + git_len : cmd_idx]
  135:                 tokens = [t for t in gap.strip().split() if t]
  136:                 only_flags_and_args = True
  137:                 expect_flag_arg = False
  138:                 for t in tokens:
  139:                     if expect_flag_arg:
  140:                         expect_flag_arg = False
  141:                         continue
  142:                     if t.startswith("-"):
  143:                         # -c / -C / --work-tree / --git-dir / --namespace / --super-prefix take a following arg
  144:                         if t in ("-c", "-C", "--work-tree", "--git-dir", "--namespace", "--super-prefix"):
  145:                             expect_flag_arg = True
  146:                         continue
  147:                     only_flags_and_args = False
  148:                     break
  149:                 if not only_flags_and_args:
  150:                     search_pos = cmd_idx + 1
  151:                     continue
  152: 
  153:                 if cmd_idx < best_idx:
  154:                     best_idx = cmd_idx
  155:                     best_cmd = cmd
  156:                 break
  157: 
  158:         if best_cmd is not None:
  159:             return (best_cmd, best_idx + len(best_cmd))
  160:         start = git_idx + git_len
  161:     return None
  162: 
  163: 
  164: def _strip_quoted_regions(cmd: str) -> str:
  165:     """Replace quoted-string contents with a placeholder so pattern matchers
  166:     see shell structure without matching inside quoted narrative data.
  167: 
  168:     Closes parent cycle-184 commit-narrative false-positive where `git commit -m
  169:     "note about --no-verify"` triggered the hook despite the flag-string being
  170:     inside a quoted -m message body.
  171:     """
  172:     return re.sub(r"'[^']*'", "'X'", re.sub(r'"[^"]*"', '"X"', cmd))
  173: 
  174: 
  175: def _has_no_verify_flag(s: str, command: str, offset: int) -> bool:
  176:     """--no-verify in region after the subcommand, plus -n for commit.
  177: 
  178:     Region is quote-stripped before search so `git commit -m "note about --no-verify"`
  179:     (narrative in -m) no longer false-positives. Real flags (`git commit --no-verify`)
  180:     stay caught.
  181:     """
  182:     region = _strip_quoted_regions(s[offset:])
  183:     if _RE_NO_VERIFY.search(region):
  184:         return True
  185:     return command == "commit" and bool(
  186:         _RE_COMMIT_N_SHORT_A.search(region) or _RE_COMMIT_N_SHORT_B.search(region)
  187:     )
  188: 
  189: 
  190: def _has_hooks_path_override(s: str) -> bool:
  191:     """-c core.hooksPath= anywhere in the command."""
  192:     return bool(_RE_HOOKS_PATH.search(s))
  193: 
  194: 
  195: def _check_command(s: str) -> tuple[bool, str]:
  196:     """Return (blocked, reason)."""
  197:     detected = _detect_git_command(s)
  198:     if not detected:
  199:         return (False, "")
  200:     cmd, offset = detected
  201:     if _has_no_verify_flag(s, cmd, offset):
  202:         return (
  203:             True,
  204:             f"BLOCKED: --no-verify flag is not allowed with git {cmd}. Git hooks must not be bypassed.",
  205:         )
  206:     if _has_hooks_path_override(s):
  207:         return (
  208:             True,
  209:             f"BLOCKED: Overriding core.hooksPath is not allowed with git {cmd}. Git hooks must not be bypassed.",
  210:         )
  211:     return (False, "")
  212: 
  213: 
  214: def _extract_command(raw: str) -> str:
  215:     """Pull command from JSON payload or return raw."""
  216:     trimmed = raw.strip()
  217:     if not trimmed.startswith("{"):
  218:         return trimmed
  219:     try:
  220:         parsed = json.loads(trimmed)

    7: # SOTA Research Architecture (SRA) — multi-dimensional convergence gate
    8: 
    9: # Reference: TIER-1-DIRECT user directive 2026-05-08 verbatim "improve your research architecture, you need to make sure they have the ability to gather muti dimensional informaiton, github and beyond, to find the convergence, it is the very foundation of our entire architecutre" — codifies the methodology improvement mandate triggered by Wave 102 audit's over-applied REJECT verdicts (Ship 2T trufflehog AGPL-3.0 over-applied to CLI-binary-use; KuzuDB recommended at 7-month-stale despite "SOTA" framing).
   10: 
   11: # Reference: TIER-2 sister `Z:/claude-sota/.claude/rules/convergence-gate.md` — Axis-1+2+3 convergence-gate (org-distinct + named-T2 + ≥3-month stable). SRA EXTENDS that 3-axis gate to 10-dimension convergence with use-class precision.
   12: 
   13: # Reference: TIER-2 sister `Z:/claude-sota/.claude/rules/agent-harness-fit-verification.md` Probe 6 license-blocker — SRA D1 dimension is the use-class-precise refinement of Probe 6 (Probe 6 is blanket REJECT on AGPL/GPL/SSPL; SRA D1 distinguishes CLI-binary-use vs library-link vs network-served vs SaaS-distributed).
   14: 
   15: ## The rule
   16: 
   17: A repo qualifies as **SOTA** for eee runtime adoption if and only if it satisfies **multi-dimensional convergence** across 10 independent dimensions, with **use-class precision** per dimension. Flat criteria ("AGPL = REJECT" / "stars >500") produce false-positive rejects + miss real risk. Convergence gate = ≥7 of 10 dimensions PASS for use-class, with no critical dimension (D1 license-use-class blocking, D6 use-class incompatible) FAILED.
   18: 
   19: **Replacement viability**: any proposed replacement MUST satisfy D1-D10 AND be ≤ incumbent's last-push age (D2 freshness gate). A staler replacement is NOT a valid SOTA recommendation.
   20: 
   21: ## When this rule applies
   22: 
   23: ANY of these triggers fires SRA:
   24: 
   25: 1. Architecture audit identifying REJECT/DOWNGRADE candidate
   26: 2. New repo/dep adoption decision
   27: 3. Replacement of existing dep with alternative
   28: 4. Plugin install candidate evaluation
   29: 5. License-context question (any non-MIT / non-Apache / non-BSD license)
   30: 6. SOTA-freshness verification of any cite anchor
   31: 7. Named-author endorsement claim verification
   32: 
   33: ## The 10 dimensions
   34: 
   35: ### D1 — License-use-class precision
   36: 
   37: Distinguish use-class BEFORE applying license clauses. License clause activation per sub-class:
   38: 
   39: | License | CLI-binary-use | Library-link | Network-served | SaaS-distributed |
   40: |---|---|---|---|---|
   41: | MIT / Apache-2.0 / BSD | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
   42: | LGPL-2.1/3.0 | ✅ | dynamic-link OK; static-link infects | ✅ | ✅ |
   43: | GPL-2.0/3.0 | ✅ (no source-distribute mandate) | infects derivative | requires source-disclosure | full GPL-class restrictions |
   44: | AGPL-3.0 | ✅ (local-CLI use) | infects derivative + network-trigger | requires source-disclosure | full AGPL-class restrictions |
   45: | SSPL-1.0 | ✅ (local DB) | ✅ | ✅ | restricts SaaS-as-product |
   46: | Elastic License 2.0 (ELv2) | ✅ (local plugin) | ✅ | ✅ | restricts managed-service-resale |
   47: | Proprietary (commercial) | per-license-terms | per-license-terms | per-license-terms | per-license-terms |
   48: | **NO LICENSE FILE** | undefined; default copyright; technically no permission to use | undefined | undefined | undefined |
   49: 
   50: **Probe 6 application** is use-class-aware:
   51: - AGPL CLI binary used to scan local files = ✅ ACCEPTABLE for eee
   52: - AGPL library linked into eee runtime code = ❌ REJECT (license infects derivative)
   53: - AGPL network-served as part of eee = ❌ REJECT (requires source-disclosure)
   54: - ELv2 plugin loaded into eee runtime = ✅ ACCEPTABLE (eee is not SaaS-resale)
   55: - SSPL DB used as local backend = ✅ ACCEPTABLE (eee is not DB-as-a-service product)
   56: 
   57: **eee use-class baseline**: local autonomous /loop runtime; NOT distributed-as-product; NOT network-hosted-for-third-parties; NOT SaaS-resale. This use-class makes most non-permissive licenses ACCEPTABLE for inclusion (with disclosure).
   58: 
   59: ### D2 — SOTA-freshness gate (replacement-must-be-more-current)
   60: 
   61: For any proposed REPLACEMENT:
   62: - Compute `incumbent_last_push_age` = (now - incumbent's pushed_at)
   63: - Compute `replacement_last_push_age` = (now - replacement's pushed_at)
   64: - **MUST**: replacement_last_push_age ≤ incumbent_last_push_age
   65: - IF replacement is staler than incumbent → REJECT REPLACEMENT, keep incumbent
   66: 
   67: For incumbents:
   68: - last-push < 30 days = ACTIVE
   69: - 30-90 days = MAINTAINED
   70: - 90-180 days = STABLE-BURN-IN (acceptable for mature deps)
   71: - 180-365 days = STALE (DOWNGRADE flag)
   72: - > 365 days = DORMANT (REJECT unless explicit ABANDONED-BUT-WORKING justification)
   73: 
   74: ### D3 — Star-velocity vs content-depth (fresh-paint detection)
   75: 
   76: Calculate signals:
   77: - `velocity = stars / age-days`
   78: - `density = repo-size-KB / max(stars, 1)`
   79: 
   80: Anti-pattern signals:

   31: # Advanced agent team E2E unleashed — standing directive
   32: 
   33: ## The rule
   34: 
   35: Every non-trivial fire (architecture audit / SOTA convergence / token-eff investigation / cross-model verification / gap-resolution wave) MUST spawn a 3-5 agent team. **Scope**: output fires only — rule-edit fires are governed by `cross-model-consensus.md` T1/T2/T3 gates alone, not this standing directive. **CADP cap**: concurrent dispatch is bounded by `parallel-agent-wave.md §CADP rule 2` (max 3 concurrent unless `python Z:/claude/ccc/tools/status.py` shows cache ≥50% verified); 4-5 agents MUST use staggered dispatch — see §Anti-patterns for the full CADP carve-out. The team MUST satisfy ALL of:
   36: 
   37: 1. **GPT-5.5 BRIDGE-MODE for ≥2 agents** — `codex-rescue` / `gpt5-reviewer` / `gpt5-archaeologist` (Sonnet wrapper invoking real GPT-5.5 via codex CLI); satisfies cross-model-asymmetry per `cross-model-consensus.md`. **Per-call codex time-budget mandate** (Wave 44 FM-17.d codification, refined Wave 45 Fire 1 per codex T1 NEEDS-REVISION conf=0.84 Pattern A): each codex call within agent brief MUST budget time per call -- **default 90s, normal cap 120s, 180s only with explicit reason**. Bounded, independently answerable calls preferred over one xhigh open-ended call when the question decomposes cleanly; keep one call when setup/context dominates OR the answer requires integrated judgment. Wrapper stream-watchdog 600s timeout fires before xhigh codex completion (empirical 5-15min per `cross-model-consensus.md §Profile selection rule`); short-call budget bypasses watchdog OR enables main-session foreground+tee fallback per `fm17-subagent-fleet-depletion.md §FM-17.d` recovery
   38: 2. **Brief cites SOTA repos at file:line depth** — every claim in the agent brief carries `Z:/repos/deps/<repo>/<file>:<line> @ HEAD <SHA>` OR `code.claude.com/docs/...` OR `mcp__github__get_file_contents` result; agent briefs ARE inputs to the agent's reasoning per `feedback_agent_team_brief_must_cite_sota_repos_at_file_line_2026_05_02.md`
   39: 3. **Line-by-line SOTA repo audit mandate** — for adoption-class waves, agents must Read the candidate repo's relevant `<file>` end-to-end (NOT skim README); Probe DAG 1-7 per `agent-harness-fit-verification.md`
   40: 4. **Anthropic official docs as authority guide** — `code.claude.com/docs/en/*` is TIER-1 LIVING-AUTHORITY per `cross-model-consensus.md` Normative Authority Map; CCBP `Z:/repos/deps/claude-code-best-practice-shan/` HEAD-pinned is TIER-2 third-party reinforcement
   41: 5. **ARTIFACT-INLINE per FM-19** — Bash-only / no-Write agents (architect / gpt5-reviewer / gpt5-archaeologist / code-reviewer) embed `## ARTIFACT-INLINE: tmp/wave<N>-<agent>-<topic>-<date>.md` in final return; orchestrator persists post-completion per `fm19-readonly-guard-sidestep.md`
   42: 6. **Mia pre-apply on returned prescriptions** — every prescription with `prescribed_edits` / specific file:line claims gets cheap-probe verification BEFORE Edit per `mia-pre-apply.md` (28/29 broad-fan-out prescriptions catch as OVER-claims pre-apply per Mia n=29 ladder)
   43: 7. **Forward-only persistence** — output paths follow `tmp/wave<N>-<agent>-<topic>-<date>.md` convention; orchestrator-side `mv` to canonical path (gitignored per `.gitignore:216`); reference memory files for cross-arc evidence
   44: 8. **OUTPUT_BUDGET and TERMINATION in every brief** — every agent brief MUST include `OUTPUT_BUDGET: <max LOC | max words>` (bounds artifact size for orchestrator ingestion per `team-orchestration.md §OUTPUT_BUDGET semantic`) AND `TERMINATION: on_handoff_to: orchestrator | max_turns: N | terminationCondition: <predicates>` per `team-orchestration.md §Termination contract`
